p: The ad opens on a terminal showing a generated spec file and asks who reviews it. It then transitions to a web artifact where feedback is highlighted, followed by Claude CLI applying comments to update the metrics on the same URL before concluding with a CTA.
Artifact Share lets teams review and comment on AI-generated specs, which agents can then update directly at the same URL.

[{"timestamp":"00:00","observation":"Hook displays spec file name with kinetic typography asking 'Who reviews it?'."},{"timestamp":"00:04","observation":"Transitions to artifact document with estimated delivery metrics."},{"timestamp":"00:06","observation":"Text selection interaction highlights requirement change to 3-week cut."},{"timestamp":"00:08","observation":"Terminal shows Claude CLI command running to apply feedback."},{"timestamp":"00:10","observation":"Split-flap mechanical flip updates numbers under the same URL."},{"timestamp":"00:13","observation":"Final CTA card resolves with logo, slogan, and website."}]

The visual narrative follows a crisp and logical progression from terminal generation to browser review and back to agent execution. The split-flap animation clearly conveys in-place updates. The audio track supports the kinetic pacing well without cluttering the screen.

p: ["hook frame has overlapping/collided text ('reviews it?' over 'checkout-spec.html' over ghosted 'wrote') that reads as garbled rather than a clean pattern interrupt","stat card in frame-3 has warped/wavy baseline text on '+11% checkout completion', reading as a rendering glitch","core message 'Humans point, agents edit. Same URL, any agent.' is never stated on-screen verbatim — viewer must infer it from the chat-bubble + before/after sequence"]

The dark hook frame is conceptually right (pattern interrupt, provocative question) but the type collision makes it look like a rendering error rather than intentional motion-blur, which undercuts trust in the first 1-2 seconds. The middle sequence (browser chrome, highlighted spec, chat request, result stats) clearly demonstrates the product loop and keeps the URL/brand visible throughout, which is the strongest part of the ad. The stat card glitch in frame-3 and the end card's generic 'Any agent. One URL.' tagline (rather than the intended human/agent message) are the two things most likely to cap CTR versus the stated creative intent.
